cut.note: SPIN does not check the model: it GENERATES a C program (pan.c) whose text lives in pangen*.h as string arrays, and the compile-time flags of that program select the algorithm (full state hashing vs BITSTATE supertrace vs MA minimised automaton; SAFETY vs nested-DFS acceptance cycles; NOREDUCE vs partial-order reduction). The cut reads the generated text, so the organs are the verifier's, and the mechanism 'a verifier specialised per model at C-compile time' is the generator's

organs.human_name: pangen1.h (the pan.c text as string literals); the BITSTATE / MA / SAFETY / NOREDUCE / BFS / NCORE conditionals inside it
organs.mechanism: the Promela model is compiled into C data (transition tables trans[ot][tt], the state vector struct 'now', the process step functions) spliced into a fixed verifier skeleton; the skeleton carries every algorithm variant under #ifdef, so one C compilation of pan.c with -DBITSTATE or -DSAFETY or -DNOREDUCE fixes the search algorithm; the state vector is a flat byte array (vsize) compared and hashed as bytes
assumptions: specialising the checker to the model (state vector layout, transition tables as data) beats interpreting the model; the algorithm menu is small enough to live under preprocessor flags
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the verifier is a tight C program with the model's state vector as a struct; the whole menu of algorithms ships as one text
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the skeleton is ~9,000 lines of C inside string literals with nested #ifdef; it is unreadable as a program and only testable as generated output
organs.human_prior: compile-the-model checking (also in Murphi); SPIN's is the 1989 original

evidence.ref: vault:spin-6.5.2-holzmann/upstream/tree/Spin-version-6.5.2/Src/pangen1.h:1-100 (structure), 2603-2614 (the comment 'new_state() is the main DFS search routine in the verifier')

organs.human_name: new_state (2614-2780): Down / AllOver / Up; the A_Root seed comparison; store_state (1380-1480) for the BFS variant
organs.mechanism: the search stack is an array of Trail records (one per depth) holding the transition taken and a pointer to the stored predecessor; at each new depth the current state vector 'now' is offered to the store (h_store hash table, b_store bitstate, or g_store minimised automaton): a new state increments nstates and expands, a seen state increments truncs and backtracks; for liveness (not SAFETY) the search is nested: after an accepting state is found the second search sets bit _a_t and a later state equal to the seed A_Root (byte compare from offset S_A+2, skipping the fairness counters) is an acceptance cycle; depth limits, hash resize on nstates > 2^(ssize+1), and periodic snapshots are inline
organs.output: an error trail or a state count
organs.state: the visited store; the trail stack (maxdepth records)
assumptions: the state vector as bytes is a canonical state identity (no symmetry reduction by default); a cycle through an accepting state is detectable by re-meeting the seed in the second search
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: on-the-fly verification: errors are found before the state space is complete; the nested DFS needs two bits per state, not a strongly-connected-components pass
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the state store is the limit (hence bitstate and MA); the depth-limit path prints 'max search depth too small' and counts truncs, so a bounded search silently loses states
organs.human_prior: Courcoubetis, Vardi, Wolper, Yannakakis 1992 nested DFS; Holzmann's implementation

organs.human_name: bstore_reg / bstore_mod (880-960; 'extended hashing, Peter Dillinger, 2004'); d_hash / m_hash
organs.mechanism: the state vector is hashed once to several words; hfns bit positions are derived by stepping x by j1+i (masked to the array) and y by j4 (mod 8); if every bit is already set the state is 'old' (possibly falsely) and the search backtracks; otherwise all hfns bits are set and the state is 'new'; an optional RANDSTOR makes storing probabilistic; the array size is the memory budget, and the search is therefore a lossy exploration whose coverage the tool estimates afterwards
assumptions: a hash collision costs a missed state, never a false error; for large models a partial search with a known-coverage bound is better than no search
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: verification of models whose state space does not fit memory, with a coverage estimate
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: coverage degrades as the array fills; hfns (default 3) trades collisions against bits per state; Dillinger's double hashing replaced the 5.1.1 scheme
organs.human_prior: Holzmann's supertrace (1987) is the origin; Bloom filters are the general form

organs.human_name: pangen2.c proc_is_safe (2251-2330) and the 'conditionally safe' comments (816-823, 1122-1123); the NOREDUCE-guarded blocks in pangen1.h (1453, 1537-1613, 2909-2960)
organs.mechanism: at generation time each statement is classified: local assignments and local-variable tests are safe; sends and receives on channels declared exclusive (xs/xr) are conditionally safe; anything touching global state is unsafe; the generated DFS, when a process's next statement is safe, expands only that process's moves at this state (a single-successor ample set) and records a proviso bit so that a reduced state closing a cycle on the stack is re-expanded; violations of the xr/xs declarations at run time abort with 'violates po reduction'
organs.input: the model's statements and channel declarations
organs.output: a reduced successor set per state
organs.state: the proviso bits in the store
assumptions: independence of local statements is decidable syntactically; the cycle proviso restores completeness
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: exponential reduction of interleavings on models with local computation
organs.failure_landscape: UNKNOWN by run (the reduction's soundness depends on the user's xr/xs declarations, which the run-time check partially polices)
organs.human_prior: Holzmann & Peled 1994 (static POR); Godefroid's persistent sets
organs.source_boundary: the safety classification and the NOREDUCE blocks; CANDIDATE because the ample-set expansion body was skimmed, not read

pressures.condition: an organism explores a product of asynchronous processes; the number of interleavings is exponential; memory is fixed; the score is errors found and (when none) the fraction of the space covered
pressures.failure_condition: a reachable error missed, or memory exhausted before the question is answered
pressures.world_punishes: exploring every interleaving; storing every state fully
pressures.world_rewards: independence-based pruning (POR), lossy stores with coverage estimates (bitstate), on-the-fly cycle detection
pressures.observable_consequence: states stored and errors found vs memory budget on a family of models with a planted error at increasing depth; coverage estimate vs true coverage under bitstate
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: a model small enough to store completely
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given the interleaving-independence oracle (the POR classification) must find the planted error with the fewest states; the full-store organism must exhaust memory on the largest family member; a bitstate organism must report a coverage estimate that brackets the truth: the world must show all three
